features: Fixed — THE NET AMOUNT PAYABLE SHOWN IN THE FORM DID NOT MATCH THE ONE SAVED. Reported on the forum: when recording an invoice with withholding tax, the «Net payable» box read €373.12, but the saved invoice was worth €373.11. On the reported figures — €316.20 taxable, 22% VAT, 4% contract withholding — the real VAT is €69.564 and the real withholding €12.648: the form displayed them rounded (69.56 and 12.65) but computed the net from the raw values, getting 373.116 and therefore 373.12. The server instead added up the rounded figures, the very ones shown on screen. Neither side got its sums wrong: they were two different arithmetics for the same number. The right one is the server's, because the net has to add up to the figures written on the invoice.

No database changes in this version: no migrations and no data repaired. The reported defect does not need it, because invoices already recorded were, and remain, correct. A second defect found along the way could however leave a €0.01 line on a carried-over invoice: from this version it no longer happens, but carried-over invoices recorded earlier are not corrected retroactively.

Fixed — ON A CARRIED-OVER INVOICE, THE COVERAGE DRAWN FROM THE HISTORICAL DEBT STARTED ONE CENT SHORT, AND THAT WAS SAVED. This is the only defect in this version that was not merely cosmetic. On submit, the form recomputed the document's gross total itself — taxable × (1 + rate/100), in euros again — instead of using the total it was already displaying. Whenever that product landed exactly on half a cent, the coverage was created €0.01 smaller than it should have been, and the remainder was recorded as uncovered excess: a one-cent line under «past managements», with the note «carried-over debt loaded without explicit coverage», on an invoice that balanced perfectly on screen.
Fixed: on a multi-line invoice, VAT was rounded on the total instead of line by line the way the recording does. Two lines of €1.15 at 22% come to 25 cents each, so 50; the form showed 51.

Fixed: on reduced-base withholdings (commissions, 23% on a 50% or 20% base) the recording rounds twice — first the reduced base, then the withholding — while the preview did it in a single step. On a taxable amount of €1,000.13 the difference is one cent.
Fixed: on credit notes, negative amounts were rounded by JavaScript's rule (−5.5 → −5) instead of the server's (−5.5 → −6), so the two sides diverged in opposite directions.

Fixed: in the supplier record, a withholding taxable base configured as ZERO was read by the preview as 100%, announcing a deduction that the save then did not apply. Found while rewriting the calculation; nobody had reported it.

The preview's totals calculation was copied identically into the recording page and the edit page: two copies free to drift from each other as well as from the server. It now lives in a single module, written to mirror the recording's arithmetic operation by operation, and says so in the comments line by line.

The project now has JavaScript tests, which it previously had none of: client-side money arithmetic was the only part of the system without a safety net, and it is the part the administrator reads before deciding. Sixteen cases, including the exact figures from the report. On the server side, further tests pin the same reference figures: if the backend's rounding ever changes, they light up and remind you there is a second calculation that has to follow.
